#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check-plan-framing — assert a delivery plan's framing was baked in, not dropped.

Walks a delivery-plan file-set laid out per `docs/delivery-shape-contract.md`
and checks the framing the `delivery-shape` skill is supposed to emit *by
default*. This is the framing gate; it is orthogonal to `bin/walk-delivery-plan`
(which checks structural walkability + manifest counts). The two run side by
side: walk-script proves the plan converts to a manifest, this proves the plan
carries its completion framing.

Four framing checks are implemented, each guarding a piece of framing the skill
must emit by default rather than the user re-prompting for:

  1. Five body sections — every node carries the five headings: What, Why,
     Completion, Assumptions, Key Risks (in any order; presence is the gate).
     A node missing any heading fails and names the absent section(s). This
     replaces the earlier story-only acceptance-criteria check: the uniform
     template applies to all node types (Completion content varies by type;
     the heading is required on all of them).

  2. Assumption tags — every list item under a node's `## Assumptions` heading
     carries a `(verified)` or `(to-verify)` tag anywhere in the line. An
     item without a tag is an untested claim being treated as a known fact.
     An empty Assumptions section (no list items, e.g. `*(none)*`) passes
     trivially — the tag rule only applies to explicit list items.

  3. Foundational work folded into the skeleton — when the plan has an
     executable-software node carrying tasks it must carry at least one
     `` `skeleton` ``-flagged task, and no node places any task *before* its
     first skeleton task. Foundational / toolchain work belongs folded into the
     skeleton task's description; a task that precedes the skeleton is a setup
     task in disguise, deferring the integration discovery the skeleton exists
     to surface on day one. The pre-skeleton check is structural, not
     keyword-based: any task before the first skeleton task fails, whatever it
     is named — that is the only deterministic reading of "no setup task first."

  4. Model annotations on every task — every task line (`` - [ ] ``) must contain
     a `Model:` annotation somewhere in the task text. This ensures each task
     explicitly names the model (e.g., Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) or tool that will
     execute it, preventing ambiguous task assignment.

  5. Non-goals well-formed when present — `## Non-goals` is an optional section.
     When present its body must carry at least one list item; a node with the
     heading but an empty section fails.

Two tier shapes are accepted:

  - **Full tier** — root contains `D<n>-*/` deliverable directories with
     `N<nn>-*.md` nodes inside (the original schema). The skeleton mandate
     applies whenever any executable node (`story`, `refactor`, `capability`,
     `migration`, `experiment`) carries tasks.
  - **Lite tier** — root contains `N<nn>-*.md` files directly with no `D*`
     deliverable directories. Used by `delivery-shape` for single-outcome work.
     Skeleton, tasks, and Model annotations are not required when the lite
     plan carries no tasks at all (the small-scale path has no task layer);
     the five-section body, assumption tags, and Non-goals lint still apply.

Like the walk-script, this reader is deliberately dependency-free (stdlib only,
no YAML library): it needs just two front-matter keys (`layer`, `type`), a
heading scan, and the walk-script's task-line *regex* (`TASK_RE`) — so a
targeted reader is more boring, and more honest about what it relies on, than
pulling in a parser. Headings and list items inside fenced code blocks are
literal text, not structure — the scanner skips them, consistent across all
three checks.

Usage:
    bin/check-plan-framing <plan-dir> [--json]

Exit codes:
    0   every node carries the five sections; no untagged assumption items;
        >=1 skeleton task; no node has a task before its skeleton; every task
        carries a Model: annotation
    1   a framing check failed: a node is missing a section, an assumption item
        lacks a tag, the plan has no skeleton task, a node places a task
        before its skeleton, or a task lacks a Model: annotation
    2   a node could not be parsed / no nodes found (seam not mechanical)
    64  usage error
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# --- schema constants (read off docs/delivery-shape-contract.md) -------------

DELIVERABLE_DIR_RE = re.compile(r"^D(\d+)-")
NODE_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"^N(\d+)-.*\.md$")
HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$")  # ATX headings at column 0 (the contract emits them there)
LIST_ITEM_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s+\S")
FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")
TASK_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*- \[([ xX])\]\s*(.*)$")  # same task grammar as walk-delivery-plan
SKELETON_TAG = "`skeleton`"

# Five body sections required on every node (order-independent; presence is the gate).
REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ("What", "Why", "Completion", "Assumptions", "Key Risks")
REQUIRED_SECTION_RES = tuple(
    re.compile(rf"^{re.escape(s)}$", re.IGNORECASE) for s in REQUIRED_SECTIONS
)

# Assumption-tag check — every list item under ## Assumptions must contain one.
# Matches `(verified)`, `(verified — explanation)`, `(to-verify)`, `(to-verify — explanation)`.
ASSUMPTION_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"\((verified|to-verify)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
ASSUMPTIONS_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^assumptions$", re.IGNORECASE)
NON_GOALS_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^non-goals$", re.IGNORECASE)

# Node types whose work is executable software (and so demand a walking skeleton
# when tasks exist). Other types — adr, design-doc, ktlo, spike, experiment,
# slo, deprecation, incident, compliance — carry no skeleton mandate. Docs and
# carve-outs have nothing to run end-to-end; a spike or experiment node *is* the
# end-to-end probe, so its first task is that probe, not a separate skeleton.
EXECUTABLE_NODE_TYPES = {"story", "refactor", "capability", "migration"}


class PlanError(Exception):
    """A structural / parse failure: the file-set does not read mechanically."""


# --- front-matter reader -----------------------------------------------------

def _dequote(value: str) -> str:
    if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in "\"'":
        return value[1:-1]
    return value


def split_front_matter(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]:
    """Return (front-matter scalars, body lines after the closing fence)."""
    try:
        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise PlanError(f"{path}: cannot read ({exc})") from exc

    if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
        raise PlanError(f"{path}: missing opening '---' front-matter fence")
    end = next((i for i in range(1, len(lines)) if lines[i].strip() == "---"), None)
    if end is None:
        raise PlanError(f"{path}: front-matter fence not closed with '---'")

    fm: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in lines[1:end]:
        m = re.match(r"^([A-Za-z_][\w]*):(?:[ \t]+(.*))?$", line)
        if m and m.group(2):
            value = m.group(2).strip()
            if value not in (">", "|"):
                fm[m.group(1)] = _dequote(value)
    return fm, lines[end + 1:]


def missing_five_sections(body: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Return the required section headings absent from the body.

    Checks only headings outside fenced code blocks (a heading inside a code
    block is literal text, not structure).
    """
    found: set[str] = set()
    in_fence = False
    for line in body:
        if FENCE_RE.match(line):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if in_fence:
            continue
        m = HEADING_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        text = m.group(1).strip()
        for name, section_re in zip(REQUIRED_SECTIONS, REQUIRED_SECTION_RES):
            if section_re.match(text):
                found.add(name)
    return [s for s in REQUIRED_SECTIONS if s not in found]


def untagged_assumptions(body: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Return Assumptions list items that lack a (verified) or (to-verify) tag.

    Reads only the `## Assumptions` section (heading to next same-or-shallower
    heading). An empty section (no list items) passes trivially.
    """
    in_block = False
    in_fence = False
    block_level = 0
    violations: list[str] = []
    for line in body:
        if FENCE_RE.match(line):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if in_fence:
            continue
        m = HEADING_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            level = len(line) - len(line.lstrip("#"))
            if ASSUMPTIONS_HEADING_RE.match(m.group(1).strip()):
                in_block = True
                block_level = level
                continue
            if in_block and level <= block_level:
                in_block = False
            continue
        if in_block and LIST_ITEM_RE.match(line):
            if not ASSUMPTION_TAG_RE.search(line):
                violations.append(line.strip())
    return violations


def empty_non_goals_section(body: list[str]) -> bool:
    """True if a `## Non-goals` heading is present but its section has no list items.

    The section is optional; when absent, this returns False. When present, the
    section must carry at least one list item — an empty Non-goals heading is a
    declared exclusion list with nothing in it, which is the lint failure.
    """
    in_fence = False
    cur: dict | None = None
    found_empty = False
    for line in body:
        if FENCE_RE.match(line):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if in_fence:
            continue
        m = HEADING_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            level = len(line) - len(line.lstrip("#"))
            text = m.group(1).strip()
            if cur is not None and level <= cur["level"]:
                if not cur["has_items"]:
                    found_empty = True
                cur = None
            if NON_GOALS_HEADING_RE.match(text):
                cur = {"level": level, "has_items": False}
            continue
        if cur is not None and LIST_ITEM_RE.match(line):
            cur["has_items"] = True
    if cur is not None and not cur["has_items"]:
        found_empty = True
    return found_empty


def read_tasks(body: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Return the node's checklist tasks in order: [{skeleton: bool, has_model: bool, text: str}].

    Matches the walk-script's task-line regex (`TASK_RE`). Task lines inside a
    fenced code block are literal text (e.g. a template in a SKILL), not plan
    structure, so they are skipped. Each task dict records whether the task
    text contains the `Model:` annotation.
    """
    tasks: list[dict] = []
    in_fence = False
    for line in body:
        if FENCE_RE.match(line):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if in_fence:
            continue
        m = TASK_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        text = m.group(2).strip()
        tasks.append({
            "skeleton": text.startswith(SKELETON_TAG),
            "has_model": "Model:" in text,
            "text": text
        })
    return tasks


# --- walk --------------------------------------------------------------------

def _order(pattern: re.Pattern, name: str) -> int:
    m = pattern.match(name)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 0


def collect_nodes(root: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], str]:
    """Find every node and record its type, section presence, assumption tags, and tasks.

    Returns (nodes, tier) where tier is "full" (deliverable→node layout) or
    "lite" (flat N*.md files at root, no D*/ deliverable directories — the
    small-scale path).
    """
    deliverable_dirs = sorted(
        (d for d in root.iterdir() if d.is_dir() and DELIVERABLE_DIR_RE.match(d.name)),
        key=lambda d: _order(DELIVERABLE_DIR_RE, d.name),
    )
    node_files: list[Path] = []
    if deliverable_dirs:
        tier = "full"
        for ddir in deliverable_dirs:
            node_files.extend(sorted(
                (f for f in ddir.iterdir() if NODE_FILE_RE.match(f.name)),
                key=lambda f: _order(NODE_FILE_RE, f.name),
            ))
    else:
        tier = "lite"
        node_files = sorted(
            (f for f in root.iterdir() if f.is_file() and NODE_FILE_RE.match(f.name)),
            key=lambda f: _order(NODE_FILE_RE, f.name),
        )
    if not node_files:
        raise PlanError(f"{root}: no node files (N<nn>-*.md) found in deliverable directories or at root")

    nodes: list[dict] = []
    for nfile in node_files:
        fm, body = split_front_matter(nfile)
        if fm.get("layer") != "node":
            raise PlanError(f"{nfile}: layer is not 'node'")
        if "type" not in fm:
            raise PlanError(f"{nfile}: node missing required front-matter 'type'")
        tasks = read_tasks(body)
        nodes.append({
            "id": fm.get("id", nfile.stem),
            "path": str(nfile.relative_to(root)),
            "type": fm["type"],
            "missing_sections": missing_five_sections(body),
            "assumption_violations": untagged_assumptions(body),
            "empty_non_goals": empty_non_goals_section(body),
            "missing_model": [t["text"] for t in tasks if not t["has_model"]],
            "tasks": tasks,
        })
    return nodes, tier


def pre_skeleton_tasks(node: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Tasks that precede the node's first skeleton task — empty if none/no skeleton.

    A node with no skeleton task has nothing for a task to be "pre" to, so it
    never contributes a violation (plan-level "at least one skeleton" is checked
    separately). When a skeleton task exists, every task before it is a
    pre-skeleton setup task, whatever it is named.
    """
    tasks = node["tasks"]
    first = next((i for i, t in enumerate(tasks) if t["skeleton"]), None)
    if first is None or first == 0:
        return []
    return [t["text"] for t in tasks[:first]]


def missing_model_annotations(node: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Tasks that lack a Model: annotation — empty if all carry one.

    A task must contain `Model:` anywhere in its text to specify which model
    or tool will execute it.
    """
    return [t["text"] for t in node["tasks"] if not t["has_model"]]


# --- entrypoint --------------------------------------------------------------

def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    args = [a for a in argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
    as_json = "--json" in argv[1:]
    if len(args) != 1:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: check-plan-framing <plan-dir> [--json]\n")
        return 64
    root = Path(args[0])
    if not root.is_dir():
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: {root} is not a directory\n")
        return 64

    try:
        nodes, tier = collect_nodes(root)
    except PlanError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"PARSE ERROR: {exc}\n")
        return 2

    nodes_missing = [n for n in nodes if n["missing_sections"]]
    nodes_untagged = [n for n in nodes if n["assumption_violations"]]
    nodes_empty_non_goals = [n for n in nodes if n["empty_non_goals"]]

    skeleton_total = sum(1 for n in nodes for t in n["tasks"] if t["skeleton"])
    total_tasks = sum(len(n["tasks"]) for n in nodes)
    has_executable_node = any(n["type"] in EXECUTABLE_NODE_TYPES for n in nodes)
    # Skeleton mandate fires only when an executable node carries tasks. A plan
    # that is doc/spec/config-only (no executable types) or carries no tasks at
    # all (lite tier with no task layer) has nothing for a skeleton to anchor.
    skeleton_required = total_tasks > 0 and has_executable_node
    no_skeleton = skeleton_required and skeleton_total == 0
    # Model annotations only apply when tasks exist.
    nodes_missing_model = [n for n in nodes if n["missing_model"]] if total_tasks > 0 else []
    pre_skeleton = [
        {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "tasks": pre}
        for n in nodes if (pre := pre_skeleton_tasks(n))
    ]

    ok = (
        not nodes_missing
        and not nodes_untagged
        and not nodes_empty_non_goals
        and not no_skeleton
        and not pre_skeleton
        and not nodes_missing_model
    )

    if as_json:
        print(json.dumps({
            "source": str(root),
            "tier": tier,
            "nodes_checked": len(nodes),
            "missing_sections": [
                {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "type": n["type"], "missing": n["missing_sections"]}
                for n in nodes_missing
            ],
            "untagged_assumptions": [
                {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "type": n["type"], "items": n["assumption_violations"]}
                for n in nodes_untagged
            ],
            "skeleton_tasks": skeleton_total,
            "pre_skeleton_setup": [
                {"id": p["id"], "path": p["path"], "tasks": p["tasks"]} for p in pre_skeleton
            ],
            "missing_model_annotations": [
                {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "type": n["type"], "tasks": n["missing_model"]} for n in nodes_missing_model
            ],
            "empty_non_goals_sections": [
                {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "type": n["type"]} for n in nodes_empty_non_goals
            ],
            "ok": ok,
        }, indent=2))
    else:
        print(f"check-plan-framing — {root.name}")
        print(f"source: {root}  (tier: {tier})")
        print(f"nodes checked: {len(nodes)}")
        for n in nodes:
            if n["missing_sections"]:
                missing_str = ", ".join(n["missing_sections"])
                print(f"  [MISSING {missing_str}] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
            elif n["assumption_violations"]:
                print(f"  [UNTAGGED ASSUMPTION] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
            elif n["missing_model"]:
                print(f"  [MISSING MODEL] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
            else:
                print(f"  [ok ] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
        print(f"skeleton tasks in plan: {skeleton_total}")
        for p in pre_skeleton:
            print(f"  [PRE-SKELETON] {p['id']}  {p['path']}: {len(p['tasks'])} task(s) before skeleton")
        for m in nodes_missing_model:
            print(f"  [MISSING MODEL] {m['id']}  {m['path']}: {len(m['tasks'])} task(s) without Model: annotation")
        for n in nodes_empty_non_goals:
            print(f"  [EMPTY NON-GOALS] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
        verdict = (
            "PASS — five sections, assumption tags, Non-goals (if present), skeleton, Model: annotations"
            if ok else
            "FAIL — " + "; ".join(filter(None, [
                f"{len(nodes_missing)} node(s) missing required sections" if nodes_missing else "",
                f"{len(nodes_untagged)} node(s) with untagged assumption items" if nodes_untagged else "",
                f"{len(nodes_empty_non_goals)} node(s) with empty Non-goals section" if nodes_empty_non_goals else "",
                "no skeleton task in plan" if no_skeleton else "",
                f"{len(pre_skeleton)} node(s) with a task before the skeleton" if pre_skeleton else "",
                f"{len(nodes_missing_model)} node(s) with tasks lacking Model: annotation" if nodes_missing_model else "",
            ]))
        )
        print(verdict)

    if not ok:
        sys.stderr.write("\nFRAMING DROPPED:\n")
        if nodes_missing:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "  nodes missing one or more of the five required body sections "
                "(What / Why / Completion / Assumptions / Key Risks):\n"
                + "".join(
                    f"    - {n['path']}  missing: {', '.join(n['missing_sections'])}\n"
                    for n in nodes_missing
                )
            )
        if nodes_untagged:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "  Assumptions list items without a (verified) or (to-verify) tag — "
                "every assumption must be explicitly verified or marked for verification:\n"
                + "".join(
                    f"    - {n['path']}:\n"
                    + "".join(f"        {item}\n" for item in n["assumption_violations"])
                    for n in nodes_untagged
                )
            )
        if no_skeleton:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "  the plan carries no `skeleton`-flagged task — at least one node must mark its "
                "thinnest end-to-end slice with a leading `skeleton` tag, foundational work folded in.\n"
            )
        if pre_skeleton:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "  nodes that place a task before their skeleton — the skeleton must be the first "
                "task; if the preceding task is setup/toolchain work, fold it into the skeleton's "
                "description rather than emitting it before:\n"
                + "".join(
                    f"    - {p['path']}: " + " | ".join(p["tasks"]) + "\n"
                    for p in pre_skeleton
                )
            )
        if nodes_missing_model:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "  tasks without a Model: annotation — every task must explicitly specify which "
                "model or tool will execute it:\n"
                + "".join(
                    f"    - {n['path']}:\n"
                    + "".join(f"        {task}\n" for task in n["missing_model"])
                    for n in nodes_missing_model
                )
            )
        if nodes_empty_non_goals:
            sys.stderr.write(
                "  nodes with a `## Non-goals` heading but no list items — the section is "
                "optional, but when present it must declare at least one excluded scope item:\n"
                + "".join(f"    - {n['path']}\n" for n in nodes_empty_non_goals)
            )
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

# Delivery plan — Automated run scorecard

Replace the manual `grade` draft/confirmed gate with an automatic `scorecard` that scores every
drain-cycle run on duration, cost, and correctness — where correctness is `outcome_verdict` pass
AND review GO.

## Goal

Every drain-cycle run is scored automatically on duration, cost, and correctness, with no manual
confirmation step.

## KR1

`drain-cycle scorecard` derives correctness from verdicts (outcome pass AND review GO); a FAIL
verdict is never counted correct; the draft-confirmation warning is gone; silent-Done (a Done entry
with a null outcome verdict) still exits nonzero.

## Why now

After each issue the orchestrator writes a markdown draft to `~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md` with
`status: draft`; a human ticks `## KR check` boxes and flips it to `confirmed` before
`drain-cycle grade` counts it — the gate behind the `… is a draft — excluded from rate` warning. The
reported pass-rate never reads `outcome_verdict.result` (`grade.py:131`), so a FAIL verdict counts as
a pass. Duration and cost already live in every run-log entry; correctness comes from verdicts the
pipeline already records, except the review GO/NO-GO verdict, which `handoff.py` writes nowhere the
run log can see. The fix scores each run from the run-log JSON and deletes the markdown gate.

## How to read

Start here, then read `D1-scorecard-replaces-manual-grade/_deliverable.md` for the milestone, then
each `N*.md` for an issue. Tasks are not pre-authored: `exec:breakdown` expands each issue into its
task list (one verifiable `done_when` and a model-tier routing score per task) at pickup.

## Tree

```
scorecard/
├── README.md                                   ← this file (goal + KR1 + tree + manifest)
└── D1-scorecard-replaces-manual-grade/          → milestone · serves KR1
    ├── _deliverable.md
    ├── N01 … record the scorecard correctness contract        · adr   ← blocks N02–N05
    ├── N02 … review verdict reaches the run log               · story · skeleton
    ├── N03 … scorecard computes & reports per-run quality      · story
    ├── N04 … CLI exposes scorecard; manual draft flow removed  · story
    └── N05 … retire stale `grade` references                   · ktlo
```

## Hand-count manifest

| Tracker artefact | Source layer | Count |
|------------------|--------------|------:|
| Milestones | deliverables (`D*`) | **1** |
| Issues | nodes (`N*`) | **5** |

Replace the manual `grade` draft/confirmed gate with an automatic `scorecard` that scores every
drain-cycle run on duration, cost, and correctness — where correctness is `outcome_verdict` pass
AND review GO.

## Goal

Every drain-cycle run is scored automatically on duration, cost, and correctness, with no manual
confirmation step.

## KR1

`drain-cycle scorecard` derives correctness from verdicts (outcome pass AND review GO); a FAIL
verdict is never counted correct; the draft-confirmation warning is gone; silent-Done (a Done entry
with a null outcome verdict) still exits nonzero.

## Why now

After each issue the orchestrator writes a markdown draft to `~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md` with
`status: draft`; a human ticks `## KR check` boxes and flips it to `confirmed` before

reported pass-rate never reads `outcome_verdict.result` (`grade.py:131`), so a FAIL verdict counts as

pipeline already records, except the review GO/NO-GO verdict, which `handoff.py` writes nowhere the
run log can see. The fix scores each run from the run-log JSON and deletes the markdown gate.

# N01 — Record the scorecard correctness contract

**Type:** `adr`. The build nodes encode this contract, so it is decided before they are picked up.

> **▶ On pickup — before N02–N05:** record the decision through the ADR discipline and run the
> plan-review gate.
> **Blocks:** N02, N03, N04, N05 — their task breakdown waits until this is accepted.

## What

Record an ADR for the automated-quality contract: remove the manual draft/confirmed gate; define run
correctness as `outcome_verdict` pass AND review GO; keep silent-Done as the hard violation; add
`review_verdict` to the run log as an additive field; treat `prep_verdict.route` as advisory until a
producer exists.

## Why

Building the correctness rule before its semantics are fixed risks re-encoding today's bug, where a
FAIL verdict counts as a pass. The bet is that two already-recorded verdicts (outcome and review) are
a strong enough correctness signal to retire the human gate. Rejected alternatives: outcome-only
correctness, where the agent grades its own work with no second signal; and a full prep-gated
composite now, which blocks every run on a cross-repo producer that does not yet exist.

## Completion

**Decision:** the manual draft/confirmed gate is removed; correctness = `outcome_verdict` pass AND
review GO; `prep_verdict.route` is advisory and deferred; silent-Done (a Done entry with a null
outcome verdict) remains the hard violation; `review_verdict` is added to the run log as an additive
field. Recorded as an ADR under `docs/adrs/` with context and consequences, accepted through the
plan-review gate. This node selects the decision; it does not re-author the ADR template — that
discipline lives in the ADR skill.

## Assumptions

- exec:review already writes a GO/NO-GO `review` section to `exec-state.json`. *(verified)*
- The run-log schema is additive: adding `review_verdict` leaves old logs reading null. *(verified)*
- No other in-flight work depends on the manual grade gate. *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** the ADR fixes a correctness definition the build nodes then encode wrongly.
  *Mitigation:* accept it through the plan-review gate before N02–N05 are picked up.
- **Risk:** prep-route stays advisory indefinitely if its producer is never built.
  *Falsifier:* if a run's correctness ever needs the prep route to be trustworthy, the advisory-only
  decision is wrong and the cross-repo `pr-prepare` producer must be scheduled.

# N02 — Review verdict reaches the run log

**Type:** `story`. This is the deliverable's walking skeleton — the thinnest end-to-end slice through
the real seam.

> **Blocked by:** N01 — task breakdown waits until the correctness contract is accepted.

## What

As the supervisor, I want each worker's review GO/NO-GO verdict recorded in the run log, so that the
scorecard can gate correctness on the review outcome.

## Why

exec:review already writes a `review` section to `exec-state.json`, but `handoff.py` never reads it,
so the verdict never reaches the run log. This is the real integration seam — `exec-state.json` →
`handoff.py` → `orchestrator.py` → `runlog.py` — and the thinnest end-to-end slice of the
deliverable, which is why it is the skeleton. The change mirrors the existing `outcome_verdict` path
(`_verify_to_outcome`, handoff.py:95). Rejected alternative: re-deriving review state from PR status,
which lags real time and needs external lookups.

## Completion

- **Done when:** `handoff.read` maps the `exec-state.json` `review` section to a `review_verdict`
  (`{"result": "go"|"no-go", "findings": [...]}`); an unrecognised verdict drops to null.
- **Done when:** a run-log entry written from `tests/fixtures/exec-state.json` carries
  `review_verdict {"result": "go", "findings": []}`.
- **Done when:** the halt/partial path (`read_partial`) and the `runlog.py` schema both carry
  `review_verdict`; old logs without it read null.

## Assumptions

- The `review` section shape is `{"verdict": "GO"|"NO-GO", "findings": [...]}`. *(verified)*
- `review_verdict` can follow the `outcome_verdict` threading exactly. *(to-verify)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** a malformed or absent `review` section crashes the reader.
  *Mitigation:* drop an unrecognised verdict to null, exactly as `_verify_to_outcome` already does.

# N03 — Scorecard computes and reports per-run quality

**Type:** `story`.

> **Blocked by:** N01 (the correctness contract) and N02 (`review_verdict` in the run log).

## What

As an operator, I want `drain-cycle scorecard` to read the run log and report each run's duration,
cost, and correctness, so that I can measure run quality without confirming anything by hand.

## Why

This replaces the markdown draft/confirmed flow and fixes the bug where a FAIL verdict counts as a
pass — `grade.py:131` never reads `outcome_verdict.result`. It reuses `_find_run_entry`
(grade.py:57) and reads run-log JSON directly. Rejected alternative: keep the markdown files and
auto-confirm drafts, which leaves a second source of truth that drifts from the run log.

## Completion

- **Done when:** `scorecard` prints one row per run grouped by `cycle_id`, each with duration, cost,
  and tokens.
- **Done when:** correctness = outcome pass AND review GO; a FAIL outcome and a NO-GO review each
  yield not-correct; a missing review verdict yields not-correct but is not a violation.
- **Done when:** a Done entry with a null `outcome_verdict` exits 1 and is listed; a clean run exits 0
  and prints per-cycle and overall `N/D (P%)`.
- **Done when:** the advisory prep-route column never changes the rate or the exit code.

## Assumptions

- `duration_seconds`, `cost_usd`, and `usage.cumulative` are populated on Done entries. *(verified)*
- The silent-Done check (Done with a null `outcome_verdict`) stays the only nonzero-exit condition.
  *(verified)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** historical run logs lack `review_verdict`, dragging the correctness rate down.
  *Mitigation:* treat a missing review verdict as not-correct but not a violation, so old logs do not
  trip the exit code.

# N03 — Scorecard computes and reports per-run quality

**Type:** `story`.

> **Blocked by:** N01 (the correctness contract) and N02 (`review_verdict` in the run log).

## What

As an operator, I want `drain-cycle scorecard` to read the run log and report each run's duration,
cost, and correctness, so that I can measure run quality without confirming anything by hand.

## Why

This replaces the markdown draft/confirmed flow and fixes the bug where a FAIL verdict counts as a
pass — `grade.py:131` never reads `outcome_verdict.result`. It reuses `_find_run_entry`
(grade.py:57) and reads run-log JSON directly. Rejected alternative: keep the markdown files and
auto-confirm drafts, which leaves a second source of truth that drifts from the run log.

## Completion

- **Done when:** `scorecard` prints one row per run grouped by `cycle_id`, each with duration, cost,
  and tokens.
- **Done when:** correctness = outcome pass AND review GO; a FAIL outcome and a NO-GO review each
  yield not-correct; a missing review verdict yields not-correct but is not a violation.
- **Done when:** a Done entry with a null `outcome_verdict` exits 1 and is listed; a clean run exits 0
  and prints per-cycle and overall `N/D (P%)`.
- **Done when:** the advisory prep-route column never changes the rate or the exit code.

## Assumptions

- `duration_seconds`, `cost_usd`, and `usage.cumulative` are populated on Done entries. *(verified)*
- The silent-Done check (Done with a null `outcome_verdict`) stays the only nonzero-exit condition.
  *(verified)*

## Key Risks

- **Risk:** historical run logs lack `review_verdict`, dragging the correctness rate down.
  *Mitigation:* treat a missing review verdict as not-correct but not a violation, so old logs do not
  trip the exit code.

input.name: Automated run scorecard
input.summary: Replace the manual grade draft/confirmed gate with an automatic scorecard that scores every run on duration, cost, and correctness (correctness = outcome pass AND review GO).
input.description:
**Goal:** Every drain-cycle run is scored automatically on duration, cost, and correctness, with no manual confirmation step.

**KR1:** `drain-cycle scorecard` derives correctness from verdicts (outcome pass AND review GO); a FAIL verdict is never counted correct; the draft-confirmation warning is gone; silent-Done (a Done entry with a null outcome verdict) still exits nonzero.

**Why:** After each issue the orchestrator writes a markdown draft to `~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md` with `status: draft`; a human ticks `## KR check` boxes and flips it to `confirmed` before `drain-cycle grade` counts it — the gate behind the `… is a draft — excluded from rate` warning. The reported pass-rate never reads `outcome_verdict.result` (`grade.py:131`), so a FAIL verdict counts as a pass. Duration and cost already live in every run-log entry; correctness comes from verdicts the pipeline already records, except the review GO/NO-GO verdict, which `handoff.py` writes nowhere the run log can see. The fix scores each run from the run-log JSON and deletes the markdown gate.

**Delivery plan:** `drain-cycle docs/delivery-plans/scorecard/` (deliverable → nodes; tasks expand at pickup via exec:breakdown).

**Out of scope:** producing `prep_verdict.route` (a cross-repo `pr-prepare` change in agent-skills-shaper) — required before prep-route can gate correctness; a correctness-rate exit threshold.

input.title: N02 — Review verdict reaches the run log
input.description:
**Type:** `story` · `skeleton` (the deliverable's walking skeleton). Node: `docs/delivery-plans/scorecard/D1-scorecard-replaces-manual-grade/N02-review-verdict-reaches-the-run-log.md`

**What:** As the supervisor, I want each worker's review GO/NO-GO verdict recorded in the run log, so that the scorecard can gate correctness on the review outcome.

**Why:** exec:review already writes a `review` section to `exec-state.json`, but `handoff.py` never reads it, so the verdict never reaches the run log. This is the real integration seam — exec-state.json → handoff.py → orchestrator.py → runlog.py — and the thinnest end-to-end slice. Mirrors the existing `outcome_verdict` path (`_verify_to_outcome`, handoff.py:95).

**Completion (acceptance-criteria):**
- `handoff.read` maps the `review` section to `review_verdict` (`{"result":"go"|"no-go","findings":[...]}`); unrecognised → null.
- a run-log entry written from `tests/fixtures/exec-state.json` carries `review_verdict {"result":"go","findings":[]}`.
- `read_partial` and the `runlog.py` schema both carry `review_verdict`; old logs read null.

On pickup, `exec:breakdown` expands the task list (skeleton-first, foundational work folded in).
